# Vantage Turbomachinery Boiler — Model BLR-B763 Operation & Maintenance Manual

**Document ID:** MAN-BLR-001  
**Manufacturer:** Vantage Turbomachinery (fictional)  
**Model:** BLR-B763  
**Equipment category:** Boiler

> Synthetic reference manual generated for the OneGrid demonstration. It mimics the structure of a real O&M manual but contains no proprietary OEM content.

## 1. Overview
The boiler covered by this manual is a supercritical once-through unit intended for utility power-generation service. This manual covers safe operation, operating limits, startup and shutdown, troubleshooting, and preventive maintenance.

## 2. Specifications
| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | Supercritical once-through |
| Max continuous rating | 1011 t/h steam |
| Design pressure | 220 bar |
| Superheater outlet temp | 549 °C |
| Fuel | Pulverized coal |

## 3. Operating limits & protection
- Drum level: maintain within ±50 mm of normal water level (NWL). Trip on ±250 mm.
- Furnace pressure: -2.5 to +2.5 kPa. MFT (master fuel trip) outside ±3.5 kPa.
- Superheater outlet temperature must not exceed the design limit for more than 15 minutes.
- Minimum firing rate 25% MCR to maintain stable flame and circulation.

## 4. Startup (summary)
1. Confirm auxiliaries, lube/seal systems, and instrumentation are in service.
2. Verify all protection channels are healthy and permissives are met.
3. Bring the unit up per the load/temperature ramp limits in Section 3.
4. Monitor the key signals in Section 6 during loading.

## 5. Shutdown (summary)
1. Reduce load per the allowed ramp; maintain minimum flows/limits.
2. Sequence auxiliaries down per interlocks; keep lube/turning systems as required.
3. Record final readings and any abnormal indications for the log.

## 6. Troubleshooting & work-order resolution
#### F1. High drum level / level valve demand saturating

**Likely causes**
- Feedwater control valve stiction or miscalibration
- Shrink-swell during rapid load change
- Failed level transmitter (reference leg)

**Recommended resolution**
1. Switch three-element control to manual and stabilize level.
2. Compare all three drum-level transmitters; reject the outlier.
3. Stroke-test the feedwater control valve for stiction; recalibrate positioner.
4. If transmitter reference leg is suspect, refill/verify the condensate pot.

**Related tags/signals:** Heater Lvl Vv, Drum Level, Feedwater Flow

#### F2. Furnace pressure excursions / draft instability

**Likely causes**
- ID/FD fan control interaction
- Sudden fuel trip
- Damper linkage backlash

**Recommended resolution**
1. Verify ID/FD fan master is in auto and coordinated.
2. Inspect damper linkages for backlash and re-tension.
3. Check furnace pressure transmitters against a common reference.

**Related tags/signals:** Furnace Press, ID Fan, FD Fan

#### F3. Superheater outlet overtemperature

**Likely causes**
- Attemperator (desuperheater) spray valve failure
- Fouled/fireside slagging shifting heat absorption
- Excess air / burner tilt

**Recommended resolution**
1. Confirm attemperator spray valve strokes fully and water is available.
2. Reduce burner tilt / trim excess O2 toward target.
3. Schedule sootblowing of the affected superheater bank.

**Related tags/signals:** SH Outlet Temp, Spray Vv, O2

#### F4. Loss of flame / MFT on low fuel

**Likely causes**
- Flame scanner fouling
- Fuel supply pressure dip
- Burner air register maldistribution

**Recommended resolution**
1. Clean/verify flame scanners and sighting tubes.
2. Check fuel gas/oil supply pressure against low-pressure trip setpoint.
3. Balance burner air registers per the light-off sequence.

**Related tags/signals:** Flame Scanner, Fuel Press, Burner

#### F5. Rising tube-metal temperatures

**Likely causes**
- Internal deposition / scale
- Localized overfiring
- Low mass flow at part load

**Recommended resolution**
1. Trend tube-metal thermocouples; identify the hottest circuit.
2. Review water chemistry logs for carryover/deposition.
3. Raise minimum flow or rebalance firing to protect the circuit.

**Related tags/signals:** Tube Metal Temp, Steam Flow

## 7. Preventive maintenance
- Weekly: sootblower operation check and drum-level transmitter cross-check.
- Monthly: attemperator spray valve stroke test; flame scanner cleaning.
- Outage: internal inspection for tube thinning, deposition, and refractory condition.

## 8. Safety
Follow site lockout/tagout, confined-space, and hot-work procedures. Verify zero-energy state before intrusive work. Use the protection interlocks listed in Section 3; do not defeat trips without an approved procedure.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | Natural circulation drum |
| Max continuous rating | 611 t/h steam |
| Design pressure | 208 bar |
| Superheater outlet temp | 552 °C |
| Fuel | Dual-fuel gas/oil |

## 3. Operating limits & protection
- Drum level: maintain within ±50 mm of normal water level (NWL). Trip on ±250 mm.
- Furnace pressure: -2.5 to +2.5 kPa. MFT (master fuel trip) outside ±3.5 kPa.
- Superheater outlet temperature must not exceed the design limit for more than 15 minutes.
- Minimum firing rate 25% MCR to maintain stable flame and circulation.

## 4. Startup (summary)
1. Confirm auxiliaries, lube/seal systems, and instrumentation are in service.
2. Verify all protection channels are healthy and permissives are met.
3. Bring the unit up per the load/temperature ramp limits in Section 3.
4. Monitor the key signals in Section 6 during loading.

## 5. Shutdown (summary)
1. Reduce load per the allowed ramp; maintain minimum flows/limits.
2. Sequence auxiliaries down per interlocks; keep lube/turning systems as required.
3. Record final readings and any abnormal indications for the log.

## 6. Troubleshooting & work-order resolution
#### F1. High drum level / level valve demand saturating

**Likely causes**
- Feedwater control valve stiction or miscalibration
- Shrink-swell during rapid load change
- Failed level transmitter (reference leg)

**Recommended resolution**
1. Switch three-element control to manual and stabilize level.
2. Compare all three drum-level transmitters; reject the outlier.
3. Stroke-test the feedwater control valve for stiction; recalibrate positioner.
4. If transmitter reference leg is suspect, refill/verify the condensate pot.

**Related tags/signals:** Heater Lvl Vv, Drum Level, Feedwater Flow

#### F2. Furnace pressure excursions / draft instability

**Likely causes**
- ID/FD fan control interaction
- Sudden fuel trip
- Damper linkage backlash

**Recommended resolution**
1. Verify ID/FD fan master is in auto and coordinated.
2. Inspect damper linkages for backlash and re-tension.
3. Check furnace pressure transmitters against a common reference.

**Related tags/signals:** Furnace Press, ID Fan, FD Fan

- Fouled/fireside slagging shifting heat absorption
- Excess air / burner tilt

3. Schedule sootblowing of the affected superheater bank.

**Related tags/signals:** SH Outlet Temp, Spray Vv, O2

**Likely causes**
- Flame scanner fouling
- Fuel supply pressure dip
- Burner air register maldistribution

**Recommended resolution**
1. Clean/verify flame scanners and sighting tubes.
2. Check fuel gas/oil supply pressure against low-pressure trip setpoint.
3. Balance burner air registers per the light-off sequence.

**Related tags/signals:** Flame Scanner, Fuel Press, Burner

**Likely causes**
- Internal deposition / scale
- Localized overfiring
- Low mass flow at part load

**Recommended resolution**
1. Trend tube-metal thermocouples; identify the hottest circuit.
2. Review water chemistry logs for carryover/deposition.
3. Raise minimum flow or rebalance firing to protect the circuit.

**Related tags/signals:** Tube Metal Temp, Steam Flow

- Weekly: sootblower operation check and drum-level transmitter cross-check.
- Monthly: attemperator spray valve stroke test; flame scanner cleaning.
- Outage: internal inspection for tube thinning, deposition, and refractory condition.

## 8. Safety

The boiler covered by this manual is a natural circulation drum unit intended for utility power-generation service. This manual covers safe operation, operating limits, startup and shutdown, troubleshooting, and preventive maintenance.

## 2. Specifications
| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | Natural circulation drum |
| Max continuous rating | 1092 t/h steam |
| Design pressure | 194 bar |
| Superheater outlet temp | 549 °C |
| Fuel | Dual-fuel gas/oil |

## 3. Operating limits & protection
- Drum level: maintain within ±50 mm of normal water level (NWL). Trip on ±250 mm.
- Furnace pressure: -2.5 to +2.5 kPa. MFT (master fuel trip) outside ±3.5 kPa.
- Superheater outlet temperature must not exceed the design limit for more than 15 minutes.
- Minimum firing rate 25% MCR to maintain stable flame and circulation.

## 4. Startup (summary)
1. Confirm auxiliaries, lube/seal systems, and instrumentation are in service.
2. Verify all protection channels are healthy and permissives are met.
3. Bring the unit up per the load/temperature ramp limits in Section 3.
4. Monitor the key signals in Section 6 during loading.

## 5. Shutdown (summary)
1. Reduce load per the allowed ramp; maintain minimum flows/limits.
2. Sequence auxiliaries down per interlocks; keep lube/turning systems as required.
3. Record final readings and any abnormal indications for the log.

## 6. Troubleshooting & work-order resolution
#### F1. High drum level / level valve demand saturating

**Likely causes**
- Feedwater control valve stiction or miscalibration
- Shrink-swell during rapid load change
- Failed level transmitter (reference leg)

**Recommended resolution**
1. Switch three-element control to manual and stabilize level.
2. Compare all three drum-level transmitters; reject the outlier.
3. Stroke-test the feedwater control valve for stiction; recalibrate positioner.
4. If transmitter reference leg is suspect, refill/verify the condensate pot.

**Related tags/signals:** Heater Lvl Vv, Drum Level, Feedwater Flow

#### F2. Furnace pressure excursions / draft instability

**Likely causes**
- ID/FD fan control interaction
- Sudden fuel trip
- Damper linkage backlash

**Recommended resolution**
1. Verify ID/FD fan master is in auto and coordinated.
2. Inspect damper linkages for backlash and re-tension.
3. Check furnace pressure transmitters against a common reference.

**Related tags/signals:** Furnace Press, ID Fan, FD Fan

#### F3. Superheater outlet overtemperature

**Likely causes**
- Attemperator (desuperheater) spray valve failure
- Fouled/fireside slagging shifting heat absorption
- Excess air / burner tilt

**Recommended resolution**

3. Schedule sootblowing of the affected superheater bank.

**Related tags/signals:** SH Outlet Temp, Spray Vv, O2

#### F4. Loss of flame / MFT on low fuel

**Likely causes**
- Flame scanner fouling
- Fuel supply pressure dip
- Burner air register maldistribution

**Recommended resolution**
1. Clean/verify flame scanners and sighting tubes.
2. Check fuel gas/oil supply pressure against low-pressure trip setpoint.
3. Balance burner air registers per the light-off sequence.

**Related tags/signals:** Flame Scanner, Fuel Press, Burner

#### F5. Rising tube-metal temperatures

**Likely causes**
- Internal deposition / scale
- Localized overfiring
- Low mass flow at part load

**Recommended resolution**
1. Trend tube-metal thermocouples; identify the hottest circuit.
2. Review water chemistry logs for carryover/deposition.
3. Raise minimum flow or rebalance firing to protect the circuit.

**Related tags/signals:** Tube Metal Temp, Steam Flow

- Weekly: sootblower operation check and drum-level transmitter cross-check.
- Monthly: attemperator spray valve stroke test; flame scanner cleaning.
- Outage: internal inspection for tube thinning, deposition, and refractory condition.

## 8. Safety
Follow site lockout/tagout, confined-space, and hot-work procedures. Verify zero-energy state before intrusive work. Use the protection interlocks listed in Section 3; do not defeat trips without an approved procedure.

# Vantage Turbomachinery Boiler Feed Pump — Model BFP-B763 Operation & Maintenance Manual

**Document ID:** MAN-BFP-001  
**Manufacturer:** Vantage Turbomachinery (fictional)  
**Model:** BFP-B763  
**Equipment category:** Boiler Feed Pump

> Synthetic reference manual generated for the OneGrid demonstration. It mimics the structure of a real O&M manual but contains no proprietary OEM content.

## 1. Overview
The boiler feed pump covered by this manual is a multistage barrel (bb5) unit intended for utility power-generation service. This manual covers safe operation, operating limits, startup and shutdown, troubleshooting, and preventive maintenance.

## 2. Specifications
| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | Multistage barrel (BB5) |
| Rated flow | 1182 m³/h |
| Rated head | 2854 m |
| Driver | Variable-speed electric + hydraulic coupling |
| Seal | Mechanical cartridge seal |

## 3. Operating limits & protection
- Minimum continuous flow: keep above the recirculation setpoint to prevent thermal damage.
- Suction pressure must stay above NPSH-required margin to avoid cavitation.
- Bearing temperature alarm 90 °C, trip 100 °C. Vibration alarm 4.5 mm/s, trip 7.1 mm/s.

## 4. Startup (summary)
1. Confirm auxiliaries, lube/seal systems, and instrumentation are in service.
2. Verify all protection channels are healthy and permissives are met.
3. Bring the unit up per the load/temperature ramp limits in Section 3.
4. Monitor the key signals in Section 6 during loading.

## 5. Shutdown (summary)
1. Reduce load per the allowed ramp; maintain minimum flows/limits.
2. Sequence auxiliaries down per interlocks; keep lube/turning systems as required.
3. Record final readings and any abnormal indications for the log.

## 6. Troubleshooting & work-order resolution
#### F1. High vibration on the pump / driver train

**Likely causes**
- Coupling misalignment
- Rotor unbalance or bowed shaft
- Bearing wear or oil-whirl
- Cavitation from low suction

**Recommended resolution**
1. Confirm the reading on a second channel; check for looseness first.
2. Verify hot alignment; re-shim if offset exceeds tolerance.
3. Check suction pressure/NPSH margin; open recirc if starved.
4. Inspect journal bearings and oil supply temperature/pressure.

**Related tags/signals:** NLOAD, Vibration, Bearing, Suction Press

#### F2. Bearing temperature rising toward trip

**Likely causes**
- Low or hot lube-oil supply
- Bearing wear / metal-to-metal
- Cooling-water loss to oil cooler

**Recommended resolution**
1. Verify lube-oil supply pressure and cooler outlet temperature.
2. Confirm oil-cooler cooling-water flow is established.
3. Trend the temperature; if still climbing, reduce load and plan a stop.

**Related tags/signals:** Bearing Temp, Oil Press, Cooling Water

#### F3. Seal leakage / seal-water flow abnormal

**Likely causes**
- Worn mechanical seal faces
- Loss of seal flush / plugged orifice
- Excessive shaft deflection

**Recommended resolution**
1. Check seal flush flow and filter for plugging.
2. Inspect seal faces and secondary O-rings for wear.
3. Verify shaft runout is within tolerance.

**Related tags/signals:** Seal Flow, Seal Press

#### F4. Insufficient discharge head / low flow

**Likely causes**
- Internal wear-ring clearance opened up
- Recirculation valve stuck open
- Air ingress on suction

**Recommended resolution**
1. Confirm the recirculation valve position and stroke it closed.
2. Check for suction air ingress and vent the casing.
3. If head deficit persists, plan a wear-ring clearance inspection.

**Related tags/signals:** Discharge Press, Recirc Vv, Flow

## 7. Preventive maintenance
- Daily: bearing temperature and vibration trend review.
- Monthly: lube-oil sample and cooler performance check.
- Annual: laser alignment verification and seal condition inspection.

## 8. Safety
Follow site lockout/tagout, confined-space, and hot-work procedures. Verify zero-energy state before intrusive work. Use the protection interlocks listed in Section 3; do not defeat trips without an approved procedure.

## 3. Operating limits & protection
- Bearing metal temperature alarm 100 °C, trip 115 °C.
- Shaft vibration alarm 125 µm, trip 250 µm (peak-peak).
- Differential expansion and axial position must remain within the OEM envelope.
- Observe cold/warm/hot start ramp rates to control rotor thermal stress.

## 4. Startup (summary)
1. Confirm auxiliaries, lube/seal systems, and instrumentation are in service.
2. Verify all protection channels are healthy and permissives are met.
3. Bring the unit up per the load/temperature ramp limits in Section 3.

## 5. Shutdown (summary)
1. Reduce load per the allowed ramp; maintain minimum flows/limits.
2. Sequence auxiliaries down per interlocks; keep lube/turning systems as required.
3. Record final readings and any abnormal indications for the log.

## 6. Troubleshooting & work-order resolution
#### F1. Rising shaft vibration

**Likely causes**
- Thermal bow after trip / uneven cooling
- Bearing instability (oil whirl)
- Rub or unbalance from deposits

**Recommended resolution**
1. Check for eccentricity/bow before restart; use turning gear per schedule.
2. Verify bearing oil supply temperature and pressure.
3. Trend 1x/2x vibration components to distinguish unbalance from rub.

**Related tags/signals:** Vibration, Shaft, Eccentricity

#### F2. Bearing metal temperature high

**Likely causes**
- Reduced oil flow or high oil-inlet temperature
- Babbitt wear
- High thrust load / axial shift

**Recommended resolution**
1. Verify lube-oil header pressure and cooler outlet temperature.
2. Check axial position / thrust bearing wear indicator.
3. Reduce load and monitor; prepare an orderly shutdown if trending up.

**Related tags/signals:** Bearing Metal Temp, Oil Temp, Axial Pos

#### F3. High differential expansion

**Likely causes**
- Start ramp too fast for metal temperature
- Gland steam / cooling imbalance
- Casing drain issue

**Recommended resolution**
1. Slow the load/temperature ramp to the allowed rate.
2. Verify gland steam temperature and casing drains are open on start.
3. Hold load and soak until differential expansion returns to band.

**Related tags/signals:** Diff Exp, Metal Temp

#### F4. Overspeed test failure / governor hunting

**Likely causes**
- Control-oil contamination
- Servo valve wear
- Speed probe fault

**Recommended resolution**
1. Sample and filter control oil; verify cleanliness.
2. Check redundant speed probes for agreement.
3. Bench-test the servo/actuator and re-stroke.

**Related tags/signals:** Speed, Control Oil, Governor

## 7. Preventive maintenance
- Each start: eccentricity and differential-expansion checks before rolling.
- Monthly: lube/control-oil sampling; overspeed trip channel test per schedule.
- Outage: bearing inspection, blade/deposit inspection, alignment verification.

1. Reduce load per the allowed ramp; maintain minimum flows/limits.
2. Sequence auxiliaries down per interlocks; keep lube/turning systems as required.

**Likely causes**
- Thermal bow after trip / uneven cooling

- Reduced oil flow or high oil-inlet temperature
- Babbitt wear
- High thrust load / axial shift

**Recommended resolution**

- Casing drain issue

## 3. Operating limits & protection
- Stator winding temperature alarm per class; keep within the capability curve.
- Hydrogen purity ≥ 95% and casing pressure within band (H2-cooled units).
- Operate within the reactive capability (P-Q) curve; respect field-current limit.

## 4. Startup (summary)
1. Confirm auxiliaries, lube/seal systems, and instrumentation are in service.
2. Verify all protection channels are healthy and permissives are met.

1. Reduce load per the allowed ramp; maintain minimum flows/limits.

3. Record final readings and any abnormal indications for the log.

## 6. Troubleshooting & work-order resolution
#### F1. Stator temperature high

**Likely causes**
- Cooling gas/water flow reduced
- Overload beyond capability curve
- Blocked cooling passages

**Recommended resolution**
1. Verify cooler cooling-water flow and gas/water temperature.
2. Reduce reactive/real load back within the capability curve.
3. Check for cooler fouling and plan cleaning.

**Related tags/signals:** Stator Temp, Cooling Water, MW

#### F2. Hydrogen purity / pressure dropping

**Likely causes**
- Seal-oil system upset
- Casing/cooler leak
- Purity meter fault

**Recommended resolution**
1. Check seal-oil differential pressure and detraining.
2. Leak-test casing and cooler tubes.
3. Cross-check purity analyzers.

**Related tags/signals:** H2 Purity, H2 Press, Seal Oil

#### F3. Excitation / AVR instability

**Likely causes**
- AVR tuning or sensing loss
- Field ground
- PSS interaction

**Recommended resolution**
1. Verify voltage-sensing inputs to the AVR.
2. Run field-ground detection; inspect for insulation degradation.
3. Review AVR/PSS settings against commissioning records.

**Related tags/signals:** Field Current, Terminal V, AVR

## 7. Preventive maintenance
- Weekly: hydrogen purity/pressure and seal-oil review (H2 units).
- Annual: partial-discharge trend, cooler performance, protection channel tests.

## 8. Safety
Follow site lockout/tagout, confined-space, and hot-work procedures. Verify zero-energy state before intrusive work. Use the protection interlocks listed in Section 3; do not defeat trips without an approved procedure.

**Likely causes**

- Overload beyond capability curve
- Blocked cooling passages

**Recommended resolution**

# Aurora Mechanical Surface Condenser — Model CND-C927 Operation & Maintenance Manual

**Document ID:** MAN-CND-001  
**Manufacturer:** Aurora Mechanical (fictional)  
**Model:** CND-C927  
**Equipment category:** Surface Condenser

> Synthetic reference manual generated for the OneGrid demonstration. It mimics the structure of a real O&M manual but contains no proprietary OEM content.

## 1. Overview
The surface condenser covered by this manual is a single-pass unit intended for utility power-generation service. This manual covers safe operation, operating limits, startup and shutdown, troubleshooting, and preventive maintenance.

## 2. Specifications
| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | Single-pass |
| Duty | 865 MWth |
| Design back-pressure | 51 mbar(a) |
| Tube material | Admiralty brass |

## 3. Operating limits & protection
- Condenser back-pressure must stay below the turbine exhaust-hood trip limit.
- Hotwell level within band; conductivity within chemistry limits (tube-leak indicator).
- Air in-leakage below the design air-removal capacity.

## 4. Startup (summary)
1. Confirm auxiliaries, lube/seal systems, and instrumentation are in service.
2. Verify all protection channels are healthy and permissives are met.
3. Bring the unit up per the load/temperature ramp limits in Section 3.
4. Monitor the key signals in Section 6 during loading.

## 5. Shutdown (summary)
1. Reduce load per the allowed ramp; maintain minimum flows/limits.
2. Sequence auxiliaries down per interlocks; keep lube/turning systems as required.
3. Record final readings and any abnormal indications for the log.

## 6. Troubleshooting & work-order resolution
#### F1. Rising condenser back-pressure (poor vacuum)

**Likely causes**
- Air in-leakage
- Cooling-water flow/temperature high
- Tube fouling
- Air-removal (SJAE/vacuum pump) underperforming

**Recommended resolution**
1. Run a helium/air in-leakage survey on the vacuum boundary.
2. Verify cooling-water flow and inlet temperature.
3. Check air-removal equipment capacity and holding.
4. Plan tube cleaning if terminal temperature difference is high.

**Related tags/signals:** Backpressure, Vacuum, CW Flow

#### F2. Rising hotwell conductivity

**Likely causes**
- Condenser tube leak
- Cooling-water ingress
- Makeup chemistry upset

**Recommended resolution**
1. Cross-check conductivity and sodium analyzers.
2. Perform per-section isolation to locate the leaking bundle.
3. Plug the leaking tube(s) at the next opportunity.

**Related tags/signals:** Conductivity, Hotwell Level

## 7. Preventive maintenance
- Monthly: air in-leakage check and air-removal performance test.
- Outage: tube cleaning, eddy-current inspection, waterbox inspection.

## 8. Safety
Follow site lockout/tagout, confined-space, and hot-work procedures. Verify zero-energy state before intrusive work. Use the protection interlocks listed in Section 3; do not defeat trips without an approved procedure.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Arrangement | Finned-tube |
| Feedwater inlet | 205 °C |

## 3. Operating limits & protection
- Maintain feedwater flow above minimum to avoid steaming in the economizer.
- Watch gas-side differential pressure for fouling/pluggage.

## 4. Startup (summary)
1. Confirm auxiliaries, lube/seal systems, and instrumentation are in service.
2. Verify all protection channels are healthy and permissives are met.
3. Bring the unit up per the load/temperature ramp limits in Section 3.
4. Monitor the key signals in Section 6 during loading.

## 5. Shutdown (summary)
1. Reduce load per the allowed ramp; maintain minimum flows/limits.
2. Sequence auxiliaries down per interlocks; keep lube/turning systems as required.
3. Record final readings and any abnormal indications for the log.

## 6. Troubleshooting & work-order resolution
#### F1. Rising gas-side differential pressure

**Likely causes**
- Ash pluggage / fouling
- Sootblower ineffective
- Bypass damper issue

**Recommended resolution**
1. Increase targeted sootblowing frequency on the economizer.
2. Inspect for ash bridging during the next inspection window.
3. Verify sootblower steam supply and lance operation.

**Related tags/signals:** Gas dP, FW Flow

#### F2. Economizer steaming / feedwater temperature approach low

**Likely causes**
- Low feedwater flow at part load
- Heat-absorption shift

**Recommended resolution**
1. Raise minimum feedwater flow at low loads.
2. Check upstream heater performance affecting inlet temperature.

**Related tags/signals:** FW Temp, FW Flow

## 7. Preventive maintenance
- Monthly: gas-side dP trend and sootblower coverage review.
- Outage: tube-bank inspection for erosion/pluggage.

## 8. Safety
Follow site lockout/tagout, confined-space, and hot-work procedures. Verify zero-energy state before intrusive work. Use the protection interlocks listed in Section 3; do not defeat trips without an approved procedure.

**Model:** APH-A699  
**Equipment category:** Air Preheater

> Synthetic reference manual generated for the OneGrid demonstration. It mimics the structure of a real O&M manual but contains no proprietary OEM content.

## 1. Overview
The air preheater covered by this manual is a regenerative (ljungström-style rotary) unit intended for utility power-generation service. This manual covers safe operation, operating limits, startup and shutdown, troubleshooting, and preventive maintenance.

## 2. Specifications
| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | Regenerative (Ljungström-style rotary) |
| Air/gas duty | 110 MWth |

## 3. Operating limits & protection
- Monitor gas-outlet temperature to stay above the acid dew point and avoid cold-end corrosion.
- Rotor drive current within band (rotary type).

## 4. Startup (summary)
1. Confirm auxiliaries, lube/seal systems, and instrumentation are in service.
2. Verify all protection channels are healthy and permissives are met.
3. Bring the unit up per the load/temperature ramp limits in Section 3.
4. Monitor the key signals in Section 6 during loading.

## 5. Shutdown (summary)
1. Reduce load per the allowed ramp; maintain minimum flows/limits.
2. Sequence auxiliaries down per interlocks; keep lube/turning systems as required.
3. Record final readings and any abnormal indications for the log.

## 6. Troubleshooting & work-order resolution
#### F1. High air-to-gas leakage

**Likely causes**
- Worn radial/axial seals
- Rotor distortion
- Seal-setting drift

**Recommended resolution**
1. Measure leakage via O2 rise across the APH.
2. Re-set radial and axial seals to design clearance.
3. Inspect rotor for thermal distortion.

**Related tags/signals:** O2 Rise, Seal

#### F2. Cold-end fouling / rising dP

**Likely causes**
- Acid-dew-point deposition
- Ineffective sootblowing/washing

**Recommended resolution**
1. Raise cold-end average temperature via air bypass/steam coil.
2. Schedule sootblowing or a water wash.
3. Trend element pressure drop.

**Related tags/signals:** APH dP, Cold End Temp

## 7. Preventive maintenance
- Monthly: leakage (O2 rise) and dP trend.
- Outage: seal inspection/re-set, element condition check.

## 8. Safety

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | Globe, cage-guided |
| Size | DN400 |
| Actuator | Pneumatic spring-diaphragm |

## 3. Operating limits & protection
- Positioner should track demand within a small deadband; investigate hysteresis growth.
- Fail-safe action (open/close) must be verified after any actuator work.

## 4. Startup (summary)
1. Confirm auxiliaries, lube/seal systems, and instrumentation are in service.
2. Verify all protection channels are healthy and permissives are met.
3. Bring the unit up per the load/temperature ramp limits in Section 3.
4. Monitor the key signals in Section 6 during loading.

## 5. Shutdown (summary)
1. Reduce load per the allowed ramp; maintain minimum flows/limits.
2. Sequence auxiliaries down per interlocks; keep lube/turning systems as required.
3. Record final readings and any abnormal indications for the log.

## 6. Troubleshooting & work-order resolution
#### F1. Valve not tracking demand / high hysteresis (stiction)

**Likely causes**
- Packing over-tightened / galling
- Positioner miscalibration
- Actuator air-supply issue
- Seat/plug wear

**Recommended resolution**
1. Run a step/ramp signature (valve travel vs demand) to quantify stiction.
2. Check instrument-air supply pressure and volume boosters.
3. Re-calibrate the positioner; relieve packing load if over-tightened.

**Likely causes**
- Trim / seat erosion
- Debris in seat
- Actuator bench-set drift

**Recommended resolution**
1. Verify actuator bench set and seat load.
2. Inspect trim/seat for erosion or debris.
3. Confirm fail-safe seating force after re-assembly.

**Related tags/signals:** Position, Flow

- Quarterly: valve signature (stiction/deadband) test on critical loops.
- Outage: trim inspection and packing service on high-cycle valves.

## 8. Safety
Follow site lockout/tagout, confined-space, and hot-work procedures. Verify zero-energy state before intrusive work. Use the protection interlocks listed in Section 3; do not defeat trips without an approved procedure.

| Field | Value |

## 3. Operating limits & protection
- Track approach temperature and differential pressure as fouling indicators.
- Respect tube-side/shell-side design pressures and temperatures.

## 4. Startup (summary)
1. Confirm auxiliaries, lube/seal systems, and instrumentation are in service.
2. Verify all protection channels are healthy and permissives are met.
3. Bring the unit up per the load/temperature ramp limits in Section 3.
4. Monitor the key signals in Section 6 during loading.

## 5. Shutdown (summary)
1. Reduce load per the allowed ramp; maintain minimum flows/limits.
2. Sequence auxiliaries down per interlocks; keep lube/turning systems as required.
3. Record final readings and any abnormal indications for the log.

## 6. Troubleshooting & work-order resolution
#### F1. Degrading performance / approach temperature rising

**Likely causes**
- Fouling / scaling
- Air blanketing
- Bypassing / partition leak

**Recommended resolution**
1. Trend approach temperature and dP together.
2. Vent non-condensables; verify flow distribution.
3. Plan cleaning when duty drops below threshold.

**Related tags/signals:** Approach Temp, dP

#### F2. Rising differential pressure

**Likely causes**
- Tube/plate fouling or debris
- Partial blockage

**Recommended resolution**
1. Inspect strainers upstream for debris.
2. Backflush or schedule mechanical/chemical cleaning.

**Related tags/signals:** dP, Flow

## 7. Preventive maintenance
- Monthly: approach temperature and dP trend.
- Outage: cleaning and (shell-and-tube) eddy-current inspection.

## 8. Safety
Follow site lockout/tagout, confined-space, and hot-work procedures. Verify zero-energy state before intrusive work. Use the protection interlocks listed in Section 3; do not defeat trips without an approved procedure.
